idiom_name: hand-written row-to-class mappers over knex/node-postgres (or MikroORM's defineEntity)
implementation_notes: No dominant JavaScript persistence library maps a class hierarchy: knex is a query builder and node-postgres hands back plain row objects, so the mapper structure is yours - one mapper module per table, a discriminator lookup that builds the right subclass for a single-table schema, and explicit joins (or a second query) for a class-table schema. The library route exists - MikroORM's defineEntity API, usable from plain JavaScript, declares discriminatorColumn/discriminatorMap for single-table inheritance and inheritance: 'tpt' for table-per-type - but it is not the default stack, so the fallback shape is hand-written mapping code.
pitfalls: Driver rows are not typed: pg/MySQL return bigint/numeric as strings unless the driver is configured, so mappers must coerce explicitly or every id becomes a string.
A discriminator map keyed by data values is a prototype-pollution hazard (row.payment_type === '__proto__'); use Map, Object.create(null) or a switch.
Loading a list of base rows and then resolving each subclass with its own query recreates the N+1 problem inside the mapper; batch the subclass read with whereIn.
